metadata.bookend_exempt_reason: Course final project film, not a channel episode: it opens on its own opening card (B1) instead of a composer cold open, has no verdict card and no Your Turn composer, and carries no channel handle or persona. It ends on its own end card (B17), not a BOUT outro, which bookend_check.py cannot exempt; that script is not called by art run or art final.

beats.narration_text: I'm Prasad. I'm building WorthLoop, an agent that watches job boards for one person. It judges each new posting, and it prepares an application only for the ones worth their time.

pieces.text: I'm Prasad.
I'm building WorthLoop, an agent that watches job boards for one person.
It judges each new posting, and it prepares an application only for the ones worth their time.

beats.narration_text: For a posting that passes, it shows its evidence and drafts a packet: the posting, the answers, and why it fits. The person approves that exact packet, or it goes nowhere. WorthLoop never submits anything itself.

shot.visual_intent: A posting becomes a packet (posting, answers, why it fits); an Approve button, which the cursor clicks: the button presses in, fills with the accent color, and reads 'Approved'; a 'Never submits' stamp.

beats.narration_text: It matters because hiring is flooded. In July 2026, Greenhouse — whose software runs many job pages — said job ads on its platform draw about 254 applicants each. Job seekers waste hours on postings that were never a fit, and employers drown in applications.

beats.narration_text: Release will need the person's approval, through plain code, not AI — the AI cannot approve for you. The approval will be tied to a fingerprint of the packet: change one word, and the fingerprint changes.

shot.visual_intent: Packet → fingerprint. One word in the packet is highlighted and changed, and the fingerprint scrambles into a different one. The two fingerprints are the real SHA-256 of the two example packet texts, trimmed to 12 characters (computed in scenes.py). The example answer uses a skill in Alex's profile (js3-filter-tool-score/resume_persona.json). 'Approve = plain code; the AI can't press it.'

beats.narration_text: The test set was locked before any tuning, and my tools are built to skip its postings. Worth-it postings are rare — about one in thirty in my last test — so twenty postings will likely hold none, or one. I'll report the exact count; if it holds none, I'll add more by a rule written first.

beats.narration_text: Five traps are set on purpose, each with its right answer written first. Two: a Staff title is too senior for Alex, who looks for roles asking three years or less. And "prefers five years" is not a rejection; prefers still invites fewer — the mistake my last test caught.

beats.narration_text: The controlled failure: I write the expected result down first. Then I change a packet after approval, on purpose. A separate check must catch it, refuse it, and make me approve again. Last, someone who didn't build it runs it from the instructions, on a clean machine.
